author: feenberg
body:
I have always favored using the year paid, but Max wanted year of 
eligibility. Both have arguments in favor. I leave it up to PE to decide 
how to do the testing, in Taxsim I will have an option to choose.

On Mon, 14 Sep 2026, David Trimmer wrote:

> DTrim99 left a comment (PolicyEngine/policyengine-taxsim#1174)
>
> @PavelMakarchuk flagging a convention question for your guidance.
>
> This is the rebate/surplus-credit placement convention (the same one open on #1156 for the VA rebate), and Dan makes a good case it should be uniform across states. The question: when a rebate or surplus credit is *determined by* one year's liability but *claimed/paid* in another, which year do we attribute it to?
>
> - **Dan's position:** attribute to the year that determines eligibility/amount. For the Oregon kicker that's 2024 (the 2025 kicker = 9.863% ? 2024 tax liability), so it should show on the 2024 record.
> - **Where PE is now:** it books to the *claim/payout* year ? the VA rebate to its payout year (#1156), and the OR kicker as a credit on the 2025 return via `percent ? prior-year tax`, so a 2024 record shows $0.
> - **One OR-kicker nuance:** unlike a mailed rebate check, the kicker is a credit actually *claimed on the 2025 Form OR-40* that reduces 2025 tax ? the 2024 liability only sets the amount. So "payout year" here is literally the return it appears on.
>
> Could you weigh in on which convention you'd like ? eligibility/determining year vs claim/payout year ? so we can apply it uniformly (and resolve #1156 the same way)? Happy to implement whichever you prefer.
>
